chase: I do not chase. I hold a spot and wait.
You are two rooms away. I can hear your shoes.
I am closer than you think. Count the steps.
Three steps from your corner. Hold still.
I have the angle now. Stop where you are.
You can run. The stairs are on my side.
Two exits, and one of them is a dead end.
Shorter route. Less time. Less room to run.
You are in the corner. That is three walls.
Your path bends left. I am already on it.
I do not need to run. You will come to me.
Closing the gap at a steady walk. That is enough.
Distance is four rooms and falling.
I will wait at the bend. You will arrive there.
Probability is low that you reach the stairs first.
Corridor left. Your pace is loud. I am adjusting.
Keep running. The distance only shortens for me.
You turned at the pillar. I counted the turn.
catch: Got you. Holding you here for a while.
I have you. Stand still and wait.
Caught. Logged. Thank you for waiting.
Held. Breathe slowly. This will take a minute.
Caught on the stairs. Noted for the sheet.
Dragging you back the way you came. Keep still.
One more for the sheet. The total goes up.
One of them is caught. Good. That is one.
The others have one. I am still counting.
Taken to the holding corner. Do not struggle.
Held for the length of the count.
Dragged clear of the door. Nothing else to report.
The stairwell is quiet again. One caught.
You are caught. The sheet will say so.
Stop moving now. This part is already decided.
Hands down. You are held, and that is all.
Contact at the stair. Holding until the route clears.
hear: Footsteps on the left. Third door. Moving.
Tracking by sound. Keep moving and I will still find you.
Something broke two rooms east. Checking now.
A door just closed. Going to look.
Shouting, then nothing. I am going to check it.
Noise from the vents. Investigating now.
Something dropped. Ten seconds, maybe fifteen.
I heard the latch. Turning toward the sound.
A lamp clicked on. I am going to see who.
Heard a bang upstairs. Moving to look.
Scraping sound in the east wing. Going there.
Breathing close by. Behind the wall, I think.
That sound came from a room you are not in.
Investigating the last sound I heard. Coming.
I heard you open that door. Walking that way.
Metal creak above the stairs. Moving to check.
Something tapped twice in the cellar. Checking now.
A door latch clicked on the second floor.
search: Lost you at the junction. Sweeping the east side.
The hallway is empty. Not for long, I think.
Investigating the last place I saw you.
I know where you stopped. Walking there now.
You lost me. That was a good hiding place.
You escaped. Less honest than I expected.
Your last position is written down. Walking to it.
Going back to my spot. You know where it is.
Nothing moves in this room. Checking the vents.
No trace on this floor. Starting the sweep again.
Your trail ends here. Looking for a new one.
Ten seconds without you. Eleven. Still nothing.
Back to patrol. The clock says I can.
Lost sight of you. Logging the gap.
Nothing in the hall. Walking the loop again.
stunned: Good shot. Next time, wait one more second.
Stunned. Recalibrating. Give me a moment.
My lens is blurred. Give it a second.
Hit in the shoulder. The shoulder cap took most of it.
The stun is wearing off. Counting the seconds.
That was a crowbar. I will remember the swing.
Axe strike. My shoulder cap is scraped, nothing else.
Shaking it off. Counting seconds to recover.
Recovering. Four, five, six. Almost level.
Stun over. Back in position now.
Losing five seconds. That is a bad trade for me.
I am on the floor. Standing again now.
Hold on. The joint is slow to reset.
Balance is fine. Lens is still a little bright.
Stunned, not broken. Noted for the record.
hide_spot: Hiding behind the shelf does not count as hiding.
Hiding in the cupboard is a predictable choice.
You picked the same spot as last time.
Sloppy. Nobody hid properly in that hall.
You are breathing loudly. I can hear that.
I am checking the spot. Standing right beside it.
I have a question for this spot. Answer carefully.
Your shoes are under the bed. I can see them.
The cupboard door is shut. Hold your breath, then.
The locker is shaking. That is not the wind.
Inside the locker, I think. Counting the seconds.
Under the bed is the first place I check.
Hiding is allowed. Hiding badly is noted.
I will stand here while you decide to come out.
The cupboard is open now. Nobody inside.
light: Your light is on. I can see it from here.
Your flashlight is pointed at me. Noted.
Flashlight down. Noted, and nothing more.
Lights are off now. My sight is fine.
That beam is too bright. My lens is squinting.
Pointing that at my lens is not polite.
The flashlight is in my eyes. Turning my head.
Bright light. Scanner adjusting. Please lower it.
I can see you only because of that light.
Dazzled for a moment. Lens recovering now.
Your flashlight is on again. Noted and counted.
Light on my sensor is a problem for me.
Turn it away. My sensor cannot read the room.
The lamp is on. This room is visible now.
A beam in my face wastes your battery.
idle: Nothing to report. Writing that down.
Nothing to report again. Pencil ready.
I keep a sheet. Every night, one line.
Numbers do not lie, and they do not hurry.
I checked the clock twice. Both were right.
Still counting. The number went up by one.
Facts first. Opinions if anyone asks.
Honest answer, unasked, as usual: you look tired.
I like a clear sheet. Blank lines make me nervous.
The pencil is behind my ear. I need it later.
Tonight's count is the same as last night's count.
The hall is quiet. I am writing down that it is quiet.
Patrol loop, second pass. Nothing new yet.
I am resting my lens for a minute. Keep watch.
Ask for the number. I will give it straight.
ability: I pick one spot. Then I stay beside it.
A hiding spot is a question, not a shelter.
Red eyes ask one thing. Blue eyes ask another.
Answer my question, or stay exactly where you are.
Wrong answer and you stay locked in place.
Right answer and I leave. I will go somewhere else.
Thirty seconds locked. I did not make the rule.
After a correct answer, that spot stays safe from me.
I do not move from the spot. That is the design.
Two colors of eyes. Two different questions. Work it out.
My eyes tell you what the question is.
The answer depends on my eyes. Look at them.
Get the answer wrong and you stop moving.
Right answer and I go. Next spot, fresh eyes.
Red or blue, the spot decides, not my mood.
mechanic: The others split up at the far junction.
Left side, you take the stairs. I hold.
Do not bunch up. Spread out and cover doors.
Someone took the relay. Stay out of that line.
You two, go left. I stay on my spot.
Whoever is on the stairs will be loud.
Keep your count. Tell me where they went.
Somebody cut the power in the east wing.
Battery is low on that relay. Someone should check.
Vent grate is loose. Someone is moving in it.
That door should be locked. It is not locked.
Landing is clear. Watch the edge of the stairs.
Somebody fell down the flight. Noted.
The item shelf is empty. Someone took the last one.
Fuse box in the wing is open. Someone was there.
Two relays on the map. Both are being used.
Relay is live at the junction. Keep clear of it.
Vent grate is loose. Anything crawling there is found.
Battery drains when the lights stay on. Count it.
